title: Hezekiah smashed the bronze serpent because Israel burned incense to it—piety praised
source_text: XLV. Sed quod, juxta rei veritatem, non solum non liceat imaginibus immolare, sed ne vel minima quidem Religionis cultus pars ipsis impendenda sit, evidenter colligi potest, ex historia quae habetur capite decimo octavo libri secundi Regum. Ubi dicitur, Ezechias Rex Judae confregisse Serpentem aeneum, quem fecerat Moses: quoniam filii Israel adolebant ei incensum: eoque nomine pietas Regis istius commendatur.
pass_a_gloss: But that, according to the truth of the matter, not only is it not lawful to immolate to images, but not even the least part of the cult of Religion is to be expended upon them, can be evidently gathered from the history which is had in the eighteenth chapter of the second book of Kings. Where it is said that Hezekiah King of Judah broke the brazen Serpent which Moses had made: because the children of Israel burned incense to it: and under that name the piety of that King is commended.
pass_b_english: 2 Kings 18: Hezekiah destroys Moses’ bronze serpent for incense-cult.
Scripture praises that piety—so even minimal religious cult of an image is banned.
